html:
The Stó:lō, "people of the river", are a Coast Salish people of the lower Fraser River in British Columbia, from its mouth up to the Fraser Canyon. S'ólh Téméxw means "our land". They speak Halq'eméylem, a form of the Halkomelem language shared with the Musqueam and the Quw'utsun.

Their life centred on the salmon runs of the Fraser, which they caught and wind dried in the canyon. In 1858 the Fraser Canyon gold rush brought some 30,000 miners up the river, and Britain created the colony of British Columbia to control them. Settlers then took most of the valley's farmland. Their neighbours include the Nlaka'pamux above the canyon and the Nooksack to the south.
